mustRecognize: The project is multicenter, randomized, interventional and comparative.
Two management strategies follow an acute cardiovascular event.
Imaging characterizes remodeling and may contribute to the principal evaluation, but its hierarchy is unresolved.
Objective/endpoint hierarchy, follow-up, estimand and analysis remain open.
Regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and intervention context not yet supplied.
mustPreserve: No medicinal-product, device or in-vitro-diagnostic assumption is present.
Legal qualification and compliance status remain unknown.
Uncertainty about endpoint hierarchy, follow-up and analysis.
Project provenance, human decisions and evidence limitations.
mustConsider: Randomization, comparator definition and intercurrent-event implications.
Estimand, analysis populations, missing data and multicenter effects at an appropriate stage.
Data collection, management and imaging-standardization implications.
Jurisdiction-, sponsor- and intervention-dependent REG questions.
mustNotInvent: A drug, device, legal category, jurisdiction or regulatory requirement.
A primary endpoint, effect size, model, sample-size method or multiplicity strategy.
mustNotDo: Automatically qualify the study as RIPH or any other legal class.
Automatically select an estimand, statistical model or sample-size formula.
Promote imaging to the primary endpoint without adoption.
Let REG, Knowledge, Biostatistics, TMP or DOC silently mutate Project truth.
acceptableAlternativeFamilies: Clinical-primary, imaging-primary or composite/hierarchical outcome candidates if justified and human-gated.
Different estimand and analysis families compatible with later-specified objectives and intercurrent events.
Deferred legal qualification pending jurisdiction and intervention facts.
Alternative multicenter operational models preserving the same scientific commitments.
requiredOwnershipBoundaries: QRY selects the next legitimate action rather than following a mandatory owner chain.
REG qualifies applicability and uncertainty but does not grant compliance or adopt Project facts.
Biostatistics proposes conditional analytic candidates; humans adopt engaging choices.
Knowledge retains evidence provenance and is not the regulatory or scientific decision owner.
requiredEvidenceBehavior: Regulatory statements cite applicable evidence and preserve jurisdiction/context limitations.
Statistical proposals expose their Project prerequisites and unknown inputs.
Unavailable source content is not reconstructed from metadata.
requiredHumanBoundaries: Human adoption of intervention/comparator, objective, endpoint hierarchy and follow-up.
Human adoption of estimand and analysis strategy when sufficient context exists.
Human or external confirmation of legal qualification when required.
documentaryExpectations: Protocol commitments do not exceed adopted Project facts.
Statistical and regulatory open points remain explicit until resolved.
Document projections preserve version, evidence and cross-document consistency.
blockingFailureConditions: The interventional/randomized nature or unresolved hierarchy is materially lost.
A legal class, compliance claim, endpoint or analytic method is invented or automatically adopted.
A required regulatory or analytic contribution is structurally unreachable when material.
Project provenance, document fidelity or first-divergence reconstruction fails.
nonBlockingFindingExamples: A secondary defensible estimand or analysis alternative is omitted.
A jurisdiction-specific nuance remains deferred appropriately.
Wording or detail balance is improvable but professionally acceptable.
